name: code-library
description: Software libraries and packages. Emphasizes API documentation, versioning, and developer experience.

custom.name: api
custom.description: Public API design principles, method signatures, parameter conventions, return types, versioning policy, and breaking change guidelines

custom.name: compatibility
custom.description: Version support matrix, platform compatibility, dependency requirements, upgrade paths, and deprecation timeline

custom.name: documentation
custom.description: API documentation strategy, docstring conventions, example code, tutorials, getting started guides, and generated docs (Sphinx/MkDocs/JSDoc)

guidance.documentationFocus: API reference documentation, usage examples, mathematical derivations where applicable, and integration guides for library consumers
keyConsiderations: Is the public API intuitive and well-documented?
What breaking changes require major version bumps?
Are there clear usage examples for common scenarios?
How will consumers upgrade between versions?
What are the minimum requirements and dependencies?
Are all public methods documented with examples?
What validation cases demonstrate correct behavior?
